entities.name: PMID:25444169
observations: Klumpers et al., Biol Psychiatry 2015;78:582–589; DOI:10.1016/j.biopsych.2014.07.034.

In two independent healthy-subject samples (n=99, n=69), threat cues activated dmPFC and other threat-related regions; threat-related dmPFC activation was higher in 5-HTTLPR short-allele carriers, replicated in sample 2.

The authors report dmPFC mediation of greater anticipatory skin-conductance responses (experiment 1) and startle reactions (experiment 2) in short-allele carriers. PubMed abstract gives no mediation coefficients or p-values.

entities.name: dmPFC mediation 5-HTTLPR
observations: In two human threat-anticipation experiments, authors report that threat-related dmPFC activation mediates greater psychophysiological anticipatory responses in 5-HTTLPR short-allele carriers; outcomes were skin conductance and startle.

entities.name: 5-HTTLPR
observations: Serotonin transporter-linked polymorphic region; short-allele carrier status was associated with greater threat-related dmPFC activation in the reported study.

entities.name: Dorsomedial prefrontal cortex
observations: Threat-related dmPFC activation was reported as the neural mediator between 5-HTTLPR short-allele status and anticipatory psychophysiological responses in the Klumpers et al. study.
